primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Pathogenic autoantibodies bind the noncollagenous NC1 domain of the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen in glomerular and alveolar basement membranes, producing rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis and pulmonary hemorrhage.
vignette: A young adult develops hemoptysis, dyspnea, hematuria, and rapidly worsening kidney function. Urinalysis shows dysmorphic erythrocytes and red-cell casts. Kidney biopsy demonstrates crescentic glomerulonephritis with linear IgG deposition along the glomerular basement membrane.
lead: The pathogenic autoantibodies in this disorder are directed primarily against which target?
correct: The noncollagenous domain of the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen
distractors: The alpha-5 chain of type IV collagen encoded by COL4A5
The M-type phospholipase A2 receptor on podocytes
distractor_notes: COL4A5 abnormalities cause X-linked Alport syndrome through an inherited basement-membrane structural defect, not anti-GBM autoimmunity.
Proteinase-3-directed ANCA is associated with granulomatosis with polyangiitis, which typically produces a pauci-immune rather than linear-IgG glomerulonephritis.
Myeloperoxidase-directed ANCA is associated with microscopic polyangiitis and related pauci-immune vasculitides, not the linear anti-GBM pattern.
PLA2R is a major target antigen in primary membranous nephropathy, which causes nephrotic syndrome rather than a pulmonary-renal crescentic syndrome.
key_expl: Goodpasture/anti-GBM disease is caused by antibodies against the NC1 domain of the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen. This epitope is present in glomerular and alveolar basement membranes, explaining the characteristic combination of rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis and pulmonary hemorrhage. Linear IgG deposition is a key pathologic clue.
objective: Identify the alpha-3-chain type IV collagen NC1 domain as the autoantigen in anti-GBM/Goodpasture disease.
